conviction_note: Q3 itself looks set to clear its own guide again (Q2 core came in 8% above guide), but this name fell on both of its prints (-19.6% and -11.85%) after core beats and raises. The stock now turns on a Q4 that consensus puts at the top of the implied full-year guide ($273m against an implied $264-274m) while the CEO says capacity is constrained. Against that, positioning is washed out: down 68% from the high, lock-up past, short interest rising, calls bid at -27 vol points of skew. So p_up is 50 and abs_move 15. The findings sum to +0.4, roughly level with the scaled 0, because the offsetting items are the honest read.
bar: Q3 2026 core revenue guide $214-216m, core GM 38-40%, core op margin -25% to -23% (company Q2 release, https://investors.cerebras.ai/node/7291/html, 2026-08-12). Estimate sources agree inside or at the top of the guide: $214.9m (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CBRS/earnings-forecasts), $215.8m (Earnings Whispers via https://finviz.com/news/416198/cerebras-faces-margin-trough-quarter-as-stocks-55-slide-tests-its-raised-outlook, 2026-11-04), $217.7m (TipRanks, 2026-11-12). EPS consensus -$0.13 to -$0.15, whisper -$0.03. Q4 consensus $273.2m (Benzinga, single source) against a Q4 of $264-274m implied by the FY core guide of $880-890m less Q1 $191.3m, Q2 $209.9m and Q3 at about $215m. CAVEAT: GAAP revenue runs about $30m below core (Q2 GAAP was $180.1m against $194m GAAP consensus), so a GAAP-based aggregator bar near $215m will read as a miss even on a core beat.
positioning_check: Short interest about 19.9M shares at the 2026-11-04 settlement, rising, about 1.9 days to cover (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/cbrs/short-interest). Earlier: 12.9M at 5.4% of float on 2026-08-19, 13.5M (16.9% of the then public float) on 2026-06-30; float definitions differ by source. Culper Research disclosed a short on 2026-10-28. Earnings Whispers bearish sentiment is 18.1%, against 2.4% before the last report. Skew_25d is -27.08 vol points (upside paid), put/call OI is 1.32 on the front expiry, and Barchart reports a 0.5 put/call on the Nov-20 options. The straddle implies 13.3%. The main lock-up expired 2026-11-09 06:00 ET. Spot $100.68 is +23% in 5 days off the $77.84 low of 2026-11-05, -29% over 20 days and -68% from the 52-week high. Not a crowded short by days to cover, but rising.

findings.finding: The full-year core revenue guide of $880-890m, less Q1 $191.3m, Q2 $209.9m and Q3 at about $215m, implies Q4 core revenue of $264-274m, +23-27% q/q, and a Q4 core gross margin of roughly 39-46% to reach the 41-43% FY guide. Benzinga's Q4 consensus of $273.2m sits at the top of that range. Meanwhile the CEO said on 2026-10-13 that Cerebras 'did not have the data centers' to take more OpenAI capacity, and Morgan Stanley cut its target $279 to $178 citing near-term data-center capacity constraints and execution. The Q4 ramp and the margin rebound both depend on owned capacity coming online in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 print (2026-06-23): fell 19.6%, attributed to a full-year margin forecast that disappointed (Reuters via StreetInsider). Q2 (2026-08-12): FY core guide raised $25m and the stock still fell 11.85%. The guide and margin line has not paid on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's Q4 number ($273.2m) sits at the top of the implied range, so consensus has not haircut Q4 for the capacity constraint the CEO described. If the market had priced a Q4 shortfall, Q4 consensus would sit near $264m or below. Partly priced: the 20-day drawdown of -29% and the MS target cut both reflect capacity worries.
findings.independence: Morgan Stanley's capacity-constraint note via TipRanks (https://tipranks.com/news/cerebras-q3-earnings-today-options-traders-brace-for-a-13-7-move-in-cbrs-stock, 2026-11-12). Margin-trough and rental commentary from the Q2 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/cerebras-systems-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/). Pointing the other way: Wedbush expects slightly higher Q4 guidance (https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/cerebras-tipped-another-earnings-beat-180600004.html, 2026-11-09). The Q4 bar (Benzinga) is single-sourced.

findings.finding: GAAP revenue runs about $30m below core revenue because of data-center pass-through and non-cash amortisation of the customer warrant, the OpenAI warrant growing with the ramp. In Q2 that put GAAP at $180.1m against a $194m GAAP consensus, the wire headline read 'revenue miss', and the stock was -15.9% pre-market. Q3 aggregator consensus ($215-219m) clusters at the core guide, so the GAAP line is likely to print about $185-195m and headline again as a miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: 'Cerebras Systems stock plummets on revenue miss', GAAP $180m against $194m, -15.9% pre-market and -11.85% close to close.
findings.why_not_priced: Sophisticated holders know the core/GAAP gap now, so this is mostly a headline-algorithm and first-hour effect. If it were fully priced, the aggregators would carry a GAAP consensus near $190m, and they mostly carry about $215m. It matters less to the close-to-close window than to the after-hours print.
findings.independence: Core/GAAP definitions are in the Q2 release (https://investors.cerebras.ai/node/7291/html). Consensus figures come from TipRanks and Earnings Whispers. Q2 itself is the only precedent.

findings.finding: Q2 core revenue came in at $209.9m, 8.2% above its own $194m guide. The Q3 guide of $214-216m is only +2.5% q/q, cloud & services grew 287% y/y in Q2 on the OpenAI ramp, and the Earnings Whispers whisper is -$0.03 against -$0.13 consensus. A repeat of the pattern puts Q3 core revenue near $222-230m, 3-6% above the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both prior prints beat the core revenue line and the stock fell both times (-19.6%, -11.85%). This name sells reported-quarter beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits at the guide ($214.9-217.7m) rather than at the beat run-rate. The whisper is far better than consensus, so the buy side partly expects it. Small because of the reaction history.
findings.independence: Q1 release with the Q2 guide of $194m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002021728/000162828026044941/cbrsannouncesfinancialresu.htm, 2026-06-23). Earnings Whispers whisper (finviz 2026-11-04). Wedbush expects a beat (Yahoo 2026-11-09).

findings.finding: Culper Research's short report (2026-10-28) claims wafer life of 1.5-2.5 years and alleges the useful-life assumption was raised between the December 2025 drafts and the April 2026 S-1. It recalculates H1 gross margin at 24.0% against the reported 29.9%. Feldman's rebuttal blog (2026-11-05) cites under 0.5% of CS-3 wafers decommissioned since 2024 and KPMG-audited useful-life estimates. The Q3 10-Q and call will put depreciation policy and the fleet data on the record inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print on this line. The report day moved the stock -4% to -10% depending on source, and it has since bounced 23% in 5 days, after the rebuttal.
findings.why_not_priced: A document-level confirmation (unchanged useful life, an auditor-reviewed 10-Q, fleet-retirement data on the call) removes an overhang a short seller created. Partly priced already in the bounce. If it were fully priced, SI would be falling, and it rose into the 11-04 settlement.
findings.independence: Culper's claims (https://letsdatascience.com/news/short-seller-culper-research-alleges-cerebras-wafer-chips-la-e92b69e1). Wedbush says it found no evidence of early wear-out or inflated depreciation (https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/cbrs-stock-alert-wedbush-slashes-155056086.html, 2026-11-10).

findings.finding: OpenAI concentration: SemiAnalysis, then CNBC on 2026-10-02, reported that OpenAI's 'Ultrafast' mode runs on Nvidia rather than Cerebras, and the stock fell 19.5% from 09-25 to 10-02. Commentary also claims OpenAI walked away from its 1.25 GW additional-capacity option, which Wedbush disputes because the option runs to end-2030. The OpenAI warrant fully vests only if that option is exercised. The call will be asked to address both; RPO was $25.4bn at Q2, mostly OpenAI.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: OpenAI news has moved the stock both ways off-print: +17-19% on 2026-08-17 (OpenAI deal progressing) and -19.5% over 09-25 to 10-02 (workload to Nvidia).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced through the October drawdown. What remains is the RPO update and any management statement on the option, which the market cannot see until the call. The net of the rest: non-OpenAI customers (Figma, Cognition, Block, GSK, CrowdStrike, six deals above $30m last quarter) and hardware ($82m in Q2) offset part of the concentration.
findings.independence: Wedbush rebuttal of the walk-away claim (https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/cbrs-stock-alert-wedbush-slashes-155056086.html). The warrant terms are in the S-1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2021728/000162828026025762/cerebras-sx1april2026.htm). Feldman says OpenAI wanted more capacity (marketcatalyst, 2026-10-15), which shares a source with finding 1.

findings.finding: Short positioning is building into the print. FINRA short interest rose to about 19.9M shares at the 2026-11-04 settlement from 12.9M on 2026-08-19, with about 1.9 days to cover. Culper is publicly short, bearish sentiment is 18.1% against 2.4% before the last print, and options are call-heavy (Nov-20 put/call 0.5, 25d skew -27 vol points).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Into the Q2 print sentiment was 2.4% bearish and the stock fell 11.85%. This is the first print with a public short and rising SI, so there is no precedent.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is a mechanism rather than a priced fact: a reiterated FY guide with SI rising and the stock 68% off its high gives covering fuel. The 5-day +23% bounce shows some covering has already happened.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers sentiment (finviz 2026-11-04). Barchart options put/call (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/options/articles/ahead-cerebras-earnings-heres-barchart-172114074.html). The skew is in the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: The main IPO lock-up expired at 06:00 ET on 2026-11-09 under the final prospectus (the earlier of 180 days or two trading days after Q3 results). Up to 171.1M shares were eligible over the full early-release schedule, and insiders sold about $395m last quarter under 10b5-1 plans (CTO 60,000 shares at $115.79 on 10-27). The stock rose 7.8% on 11-09 and 7.9% on 11-11, so the supply date passed before the print instead of two days after it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-09-30 early release (19.4M shares) coincided with an 8.9% one-day fall. The final expiry coincided with gains.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The residual is that no further scheduled supply date sits inside the window, while insider 10b5-1 sales continue after the print.
findings.independence: FinanceBuzz lock-up schedule (https://financebuzz.com/news/cerebras-ipo-lockup-expiration-investors, 2026-11-10). MarketBeat insider sales (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-cerebras-systems-nasdaq-cbrs-stock-price-up-79-time-to-buy-2026-11-11/).

findings.finding: Peers that reported after Cerebras last spoke point to AI-compute demand above supply. CoreWeave (2026-11-10) beat with $3.66bn revenue against $3.55bn expected, raised its FY guide to $13.0-13.3bn, and rose sharply the next day. Intel's CFO (2026-10-29) said data-center AI demand 'meaningfully exceeds available supply'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CBRS fell about 6% on Intel's Q4 guide (2026-10-30) and rose 7.9% the day after CoreWeave. It trades with AI-infrastructure sentiment.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy, largely priced already in the 11-11 rally. Filed small. Demand is not Cerebras's constraint; capacity is.

findings.finding: Cerebras said on 2026-08-18 that first CS-4 shipments (three WSE-3 Turbo wafers per rack) begin in Q3 2026. Hardware revenue grew only 17% y/y in Q2 ($82.1m), so CS-4 shipments are upside to the hardware line and to Q4. No independent confirmation that shipments started was found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hardware has not been the line the stock traded on in either print.
findings.why_not_priced: Product timing is public; volume and pricing are undisclosed. UBS cites CS-4 shipments as an upside driver (Fool 2026-11-02), so it is partly in the bull case already.
findings.independence: UBS via https://fool.com/investing/2026/11/02/why-cerebras-systems-stock-is-plummeting-today. Wedbush ties larger upside to a full CS-4 ramp by Q1 (Yahoo 2026-11-09).

outside_window.finding: Cerebras inference on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is planned for calendar 2027, and on Amazon Bedrock in Q1 2027. Neither has revenue impact inside the window beyond its effect on the 2027 framing.

OpenRouter / Vantage token-share series for the Cerebras provider: no current data found
Codex-Spark usage or rate-limit updates since February 2026: nothing found
Data-center go-live confirmations (Oklahoma City, Montreal, Europe) for Q3/Q4 2026: none found; WhiteFiber's Q3 call (2026-11-10) did not spell out Cerebras terms
Pomerantz and other law-firm investigations: dated June-July 2026, no new filing
Independent confirmation that CS-4 shipments have begun: none

rejected_candidates.candidate: Claim that OpenAI walked away from the 1.25 GW option
rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into the OpenAI concentration finding. Its only sourcing is commentary that Wedbush disputes, and the S-1 dates the option to end-2030.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Law-firm securities investigations (Pomerantz, Kaplan Fox, Glancy)
rejected_candidates.detail: Dated June-July 2026, nothing filed; no catalyst inside the window.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Analyst target cuts (MS $279 to $178, Wedbush $290 to $190, UBS $330 to $250)
rejected_candidates.detail: Their substance (capacity constraint, chip longevity, OpenAI) is carried in the guidance, Culper and OpenAI findings; the target levels themselves are wire copy.

baseline_tension: The baseline leans up (skew -27, upside paid) after a 23% five-day bounce, while the name's own history is 0 of 2 up on prints. My findings split between a demanding Q4 bar with a confirmed capacity constraint (down) and washed-out, short-building positioning (up), so I do not side with the skew or against it.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Q3 beat finding shrunk from +1.0 to +0.5, because this name sold both prior core beats; the CS-4 finding from +0.3 to +0.2.

Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew): the Q4-guide negative shrunk from -1.5 to -1.0 and the GAAP-headline negative from -1.0 to -0.7, because the -27 vol-point skew and rising SI argue against the negatives; p_up moved from 48 to 50.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the Q3 bar is company-guided and agreed by three estimate sources, so sizes were not capped; the Q4 bar is single-sourced, which is noted in the guidance finding's independence and kept its size modest.
Lesson 9 (segment net of rest): the OpenAI finding already states the non-OpenAI customer base and hardware; left at -0.5.
